If someone or something is described as clairvoyant, it means having the ability to perceive things that go completely beyond the reach of normal human senses — things that cannot be seen, heard, touched, tasted, or smelled in any ordinary way.

This includes things like:

  • Knowing about future events before they occur
  • Being aware of things happening in distant places, without being told
  • Having knowledge of hidden, secret, or concealed things — a lost object, a person's private thoughts, events from the past that no one shared

Think of it this way: imagine someone sitting in a room in New York who claims to see, in their mind, exactly what a stranger is doing in a room in Tokyo — with no phone, no camera, no information of any kind. That person would be called clairvoyant. They are not using any of the five senses. They are accessing knowledge through some mysterious, seemingly supernatural channel.

Example: "The clairvoyant psychic told the family she could sense their missing son near a body of water, surrounded by tall trees."

Outside of the supernatural world, people commonly use "clairvoyant" as a figure of speech — a vivid, dramatic compliment for someone who predicts things with astonishing accuracy, or who seems to know things before they happen, even without any magical ability.

Example: "Her market analysis was so accurate she seemed almost clairvoyant."

Example: "He was practically clairvoyant — he predicted the political crisis a full year before it unfolded."

Here, the speaker does not literally believe the person has supernatural powers. They are saying: "This person's foresight and insight is so sharp, so beyond what we'd normally expect, that it reminds me of someone with magical abilities." It's a way of expressing deep admiration for someone's wisdom or foresight.
Literal vs. Figurative — The Key Distinction

This is worth paying close attention to:

Literal use → The word is used genuinely, in the context of the paranormal, psychics, or the supernatural. The claim is that the person actually possesses a power beyond normal human perception.

Figurative use → The word is used as a strong, vivid compliment. The person is not believed to have actual supernatural powers, but their insight seems so extraordinary that the word captures the feeling perfectly.

Context will almost always make it clear which meaning is intended.

This word is sometimes confused with simpler ideas. Here is what it does not mean:

It does not simply mean "intelligent." A clairvoyant person doesn't just process information well — they seem to know things they should have no way of knowing at all.

It does not mean "lucky." Luck is random and accidental. Clairvoyance implies a consistent, repeating, and seemingly impossible ability to know.

It does not mean "observant." An observant person picks up on visible, available clues — body language, a tone of voice, a detail in the room. A clairvoyant person knows things that leave no available clues whatsoever.
The Feeling and Tone of the Word

"Clairvoyant" carries a mysterious, almost mystical quality. Even when used figuratively as a compliment, it creates a sense of wonder — almost disbelief — as if to say: "How on earth could they have known that?"

The word is almost always used in a tone of admiration or awe, whether the speaker is sincere (in a paranormal context) or speaking figuratively (as a compliment about someone's insight).

It is never used sarcastically or negatively. If someone calls you clairvoyant, it is always a form of praise or amazement.

"Clairvoyant" is a powerful, heavyweight word. You would not use it for someone who made one good guess. It is reserved for someone whose ability to know things — seemingly beyond all normal human limits — is consistent and deeply striking.

To understand its weight, here is how it compares to similar words, in order from least to most intense:

  • Perceptive → notices things others miss, using their normal senses
  • Intuitive → has strong gut feelings that often prove correct
  • Prescient → foresaw a future event with unusual, impressive accuracy
  • Clairvoyant → perceives things entirely beyond the boundaries of normal human senses — the most powerful and supernatural of all these ideas

Clairvoyant (adjective) describes someone or something that seemingly possesses knowledge or perception that lies completely outside what normal human senses can provide — whether that is knowledge of the future, of distant events, or of hidden truths. In literal use, it belongs to the world of the paranormal and the supernatural. In figurative use, it is a strong, admiring compliment for someone whose foresight or insight appears almost impossibly sharp. Either way, it always conveys a sense of wonder at knowledge that goes far beyond the ordinary.
